sections.html:
Ward County covers north-central North Dakota, and Minot is its county seat and largest city. The 2020 census counted 69,919 residents, the fourth-largest county population in the state. Other incorporated cities are Berthold, Burlington, Carpio, Des Lacs, Donnybrook, Douglas, Kenmare, Makoti, Ryder, Sawyer and Surrey. Outside the towns, most land is farmland.

Minot Air Force Base is the largest single employer, with an estimated 6,957 on-base jobs and more than 11,000 people tied to it counting families and civilian staff. Service members move on orders, so a seller connected to the base often needs a closing date that can be planned around.

sections.h2: How a Ward County house is taxed
sections.html:
The taxable value of a house is 4.5 percent of its true and full value. That figure is multiplied by the combined mill levy of every local taxing district on the parcel. A mill is one tenth of one percent, so you multiply taxable value by 0.001 and then by the total mills on your statement. The state's residential property tax page lays out the method.

Assessed value is 50 percent of market value. A residential building provides separate living quarters for fewer than four family units, and apartment buildings with four or more units are classed as commercial. Your own treasurer's statement shows the real mills for your district.

North Dakota offers a primary residence credit and a homestead property tax credit with a renter's refund. Each has its own eligibility rules on the state tax site. If you've been claiming one, remember the buyer must qualify on their own.

Real estate taxes become due on January 1 of the year after the tax year, and the first installment turns delinquent after March 1. The county treasurer follows North Dakota Century Code chapter 57-20.

DateWhat happens
January 1Taxes for the prior tax year become due.
February 15Last day to pay in full and take the 5 percent discount (paid or postmarked).
March 1First installment is delinquent after this date; a 3 percent penalty applies.
May 1Another 3 percent penalty is added to unpaid first-installment taxes.
July 1Another 3 percent penalty is added.
October 15Second installment is delinquent after this date, with a 6 percent penalty; unpaid first-installment taxes pick up a further 3 percent.

The discount covers general real estate taxes paid in full by February 15, and the treasurer applies it before any primary residence credit. Personal property taxes and special assessment installments don't qualify. County commissioners can extend the discount period by 30 days if weather or another catastrophe forces an emergency declaration. The same discount rule applies to mobile homes, and statements are printed to reflect the discount when full payment arrives by February 15.

A statement that never arrives doesn't release the owner from the bill. Online payment by credit card or e-check is available on the county's property tax page.

Start with the Tax Equalization office at 225 Third St. SE, Suite 232 in Minot, 58701, phone 701-857-6430. If the assessor can't settle it, take the appeal to the local board of equalization in April, then to the county board, and last to the State Board of Equalization.

A township board meets the second Monday in April. The City Board of Equalization in Minot meets the second Tuesday of April on a schedule the county tax director sets, and the city contact is 701-857-4108. Dates can shift, so confirm them each year.

To reach the state board, NDCC 57-13-04.3 requires that you applied to both the local and county boards first. You can then contact the State Property Tax division at propertytax@nd.gov or 701-328-3127, complete a questionnaire and submit evidence.

  • Gather recent comparable sales and any appraisal.
  • Photograph defects the assessor may not know about.
  • Bring your notice and parcel number to the April meeting.

sections.h2: What are winter and flood history worth to a buyer?
sections.html:
Cold here is severe enough to matter at inspection. Record lows reach minus 49 degrees Fahrenheit in February and minus 47 in January, and furnaces, pipes and roofs in older homes take real wear.

The 2011 Souris River flood put more than 4,000 Minot homes under water and sent about 11,000 people out. A buyout process afterward aimed to give residents of damaged or bought-out homes access to affordable housing. Costly flood insurance and coming changes to FEMA maps are still discussed. If your house is near the river, expect questions about flood zone status and insurance cost. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can price that uncertainty instead of asking you to resolve it before closing.

Unpaid property tax stays with the property, so it's normally paid from your proceeds at closing. The title company orders a tax search and asks the county treasurer for amounts due, including any penalty built up since March 1 or October 15.

Penalties stack on a schedule. Someone who sold in summer after missing March 1 would face the first 3 percent plus the May 1 and July 1 additions. Paying before the next date stops the next penalty, and a payoff figure for a specific day avoids surprises.

  • Ask the county treasurer or your title officer for a written payoff good through the closing date.
  • Check for special assessments, which aren't eligible for the 5 percent discount.
  • Confirm whether any primary residence or homestead credit you used ends with the sale.

A cash sale follows the same steps, minus the lender underwriting that can hold up a payoff.

faqs.q: When is the Ward County property tax discount deadline?
faqs.a: February 15. Pay the year's real estate taxes in full by then, or have the payment postmarked by that date, for a 5 percent discount under NDCC 57-20-09.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Ward County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. Online payment by credit card or e-check is available, so check the county's online payments page before you mail anything.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Ward County assessment?
faqs.a: Talk to the Tax Equalization office first, then take your case to the township or city board of equalization in April, then the county board. A state appeal requires that you applied to the local and county boards first.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if I miss March 1?
faqs.a: A 3 percent penalty applies to the first installment after March 1, with further 3 percent additions on May 1, July 1 and October 15. The second installment carries a 6 percent penalty if unpaid by October 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ward County house that still has tax due?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount and any penalty are paid from the proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can close on a timeline that suits you, and the title company settles the tax with the treasurer.
